things.title: How does the builder know a card is a person's?

options.name: Only its own cards
options.difference: The builder carries on in In progress only with cards it started itself; anything a person moved there is left alone.

options.name: Assigned to a person
options.difference: The builder leaves any card that has a person assigned on the board, wherever it is.

options.name: It asks first
options.difference: The builder writes on the card "Shall I take this?" and waits for a yes.

things.title: Today: a person's card gets taken
things.diagram:
flowchart LR
  A[A developer moves a card to In progress] --> B[They start working on it]
  A --> C[The builder looks at the board]
  C --> D[Sees a card in In progress]
  D --> E[Thinks it is its own and carries on]
  E --> F[Two pieces of work on one card]

things.title: With A: the builder keeps to its own cards
things.diagram:
flowchart LR
  A[The builder looks at a card in In progress] --> B{Did the builder start it?}
  B -- yes --> C[It carries on]
  B -- no --> D[It leaves the card alone]
  D --> E[The person works on it]
  E --> F[Want the builder after all? Move it back to To do]
  F --> G[The builder starts it and says so on the card]

things.text: To hand a card back to the builder: move it to To do. The builder takes it from there.
Found along the way: with no Planning or Blocked column, a stuck card goes back to To do with a question, where it is easy to miss and its old "started" mark stays. We fix it here.
Rule: a card is the builder's only when the builder itself was the last to move it to In progress.

things.title: Where does a card wait when the builder is stuck? Agreed: C, back to Backlog

options.name: In To do, marked
options.difference: Stays in To do as today, with its question; the old "started" mark no longer counts.

options.name: In In progress
options.difference: Waits where it is, like when the builder gives up today; a comment lets it try again.

options.name: Back to Backlog
options.difference: Out of the builder's way: move it to To do to hand it back, or to In progress to do it yourself.

things.title: Where do stuck cards show on the Factory page?

options.name: A list above the board
options.difference: "Stuck" cards sit above the columns, next to "Waiting for you": reply or give a hint, and the builder tries again.

options.name: A column beside the board
options.difference: A fifth "Stuck" column next to To do on the page only, with the same reply box on each card.

things.name: Where do stuck cards show on the Factory page?

variants.name: A list above the board
variants.difference: "Stuck" cards sit above the columns, next to "Waiting for you", each with its reason and two buttons: Let the builder try again, I'll take it.

variants.name: A column beside the board
variants.difference: A fifth "Stuck" column next to To do on the page only (not on GitHub or Jira), with the same reason and two buttons on each card.

things.text: A reply to a stuck card goes into the card's conversation (a comment on GitHub or Jira), not onto the card; the card moves to To do with "Your hint is with the builder".
The factory reads Backlog as new ideas waiting to be explored. A stuck card there is recognised as the builder's own and shows only in the Stuck list, never among the ideas.
Also agreed: when the checks stay red after three tries, the card goes to Backlog and the Stuck list too, instead of waiting in In progress.
